page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-192 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 1488 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The x86_64 architecture of the Intel Xeon processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8). These hardware extensions accelerate deep learning, vector calculations, and matrix multiplication tasks directly on the CPU. Cryptographic operations are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4n-highmem-192 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 165,304.41 and a PassMark CPU score of 131,185.99, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read speeds reaching 12,801.04 GB/sec and uncached large-block write speeds at 245.51 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and PassMark memory scores falling into the average middle 50% tier.

This instance is designed for large-scale memory-intensive workloads, high-throughput database operations, and multi-threaded data processing. It achieved a top-tier Redis SET throughput of 169.92 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 209.56 GB/sec. The high density of memory and dedicated CPU resources provides qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise databases, in-memory caching layers, and multi-threaded decompression pipelines, though the lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage solutions.
